title: Inner multiplication loop
statement: Let $x$ and $w$ be bit strings, let $b\in\{0,1\}$, and let $v$ assign natural-number values to the thirteen registers. Suppose every register is at most $4(|x|+1)$, $v(5)=v(9)+2|w|$, the bit of $x$ at position $v(0)$ (taken to be $0$ if out of range) is $b$, and for each $q<|w|$ the bit at position $v(9)+2q$ equals the $q$th bit of $w$ (again using $0$ out of range). Also suppose $v(10)+|w|\le 4(|x|+1)$ and $v(11)+R\le 4(|x|+1)$, where $R=\sum_{q<|w|,\ v(10)+q=v(7)} b\,w_q$ and bits are identified with $0$ or $1$. Then the fixed multiplication program reaches the state preceding the next outer-loop step, with registers $9$, $10$, and $11$ respectively increased by $2|w|$, $|w|$, and $R$, all other registers unchanged, and no answer recorded. Every earlier configuration on this run satisfies the program's instruction side conditions and register bound.
